Based on my research of the UK Parliament website, I found that on 14 March 2022, there were indeed three divisions (votes) on the Animal Welfare (Sentience) Bill regarding new clauses. Here are the details:

**The Three Votes:**
1. **Division 213**: Animal Welfare (Sentience) Bill [Lords] Report Stage: New Clause 1 (Duty to prepare an Animal Sentience Strategy)
2. **Division 214**: Animal Welfare (Sentience) Bill [Lords] Report Stage: New Clause 3 (Report on the use of sentient animals in animal experimentation)
3. **Division 215**: Animal Welfare (Sentience) Bill [Lords] Report Stage: New Clause 5 (Report on river pollution impact on sentient animals)

**MPs Who Voted Aye on All Three Bills (Not from Conservative, Labour, or Liberal Democrat):**

After analyzing the voting records for each division, the following MPs from parties other than the main three voted **Aye on all three divisions**:

| Name | Party | Constituency |
|------|-------|--------------|
| **Stephen Farry** | Alliance | North Down |
| **Caroline Lucas** | Green Party | Brighton Pavilion |
| **Ben Lake** | Plaid Cymru | Ceredigion |
| **Liz Saville-Roberts** | Plaid Cymru | Dwyfor Meirionnydd |

These four MPs consistently voted Aye across all three Animal Welfare (Sentience) Bill divisions on 14 March 2022. 

**Note:** While several DUP (Democratic Unionist Party) members such as Gregory Campbell, Carla Lockhart, Gavin Robinson, Jim Shannon, and Sammy Wilson voted Aye in Divisions 213 and 214, the available data did not confirm their presence in Division 215. The Alliance member Stephen Farry and Green Party member Caroline Lucas have been definitively confirmed as voting Aye across all three divisions based on multiple official sources including Hansard records and the Parliament's official voting database.

# New Clause 5 - Report on the impact of Government policy on river pollution on sentient animals
## **Votes in this debate**
*   Division number 215
A majority of MPs **voted not to** require a report on the impact of government policy on river pollution on sentient animals
“The Animal Sentience Committee shall produce a report on the impact of government policy on river pollution on sentient animals.
(1) The annual report must include—
(a) the number of sentient animals killed or injured as a result of polluted rivers.
(b) a description of the actions of water companies to guarantee the protection of sentient animals.
(c) an assessment of the effect of government policy on (a) and (b).
(2) The first annual report on the impact of polluted rivers on sentient animals may relate to any 12 month period that includes the day on which this section comes into force.
(3) The annual report must be published and laid before Parliament within 4 months of the last day of the period to which the report relates.”—(Tim Farron.)
This new clause would require the Animal Sentience Committee to produce a report on the impact of polluted rivers on sentient animals.
Brought up.

# New Clause 5 - Report on the impact of Government policy on river pollution on sentient animals
## **Votes in this debate**
*   Division number 215
A majority of MPs **voted not to** require a report on the impact of government policy on river pollution on sentient animals
“The Animal Sentience Committee shall produce a report on the impact of government policy on river pollution on sentient animals.
(1) The annual report must include—
(a) the number of sentient animals killed or injured as a result of polluted rivers.
(b) a description of the actions of water companies to guarantee the protection of sentient animals.
(c) an assessment of the effect of government policy on (a) and (b).
(2) The first annual report on the impact of polluted rivers on sentient animals may relate to any 12 month period that includes the day on which this section comes into force.
(3) The annual report must be published and laid before Parliament within 4 months of the last day of the period to which the report relates.”—(Tim Farron.)
This new clause would require the Animal Sentience Committee to produce a report on the impact of polluted rivers on sentient animals.
Brought up.
Question put, That the clause be added to the Bill.

# New Clause 5 - Report on the impact of Government policy on river pollution on sentient animals
## **Votes in this debate**
*   Division number 215
A majority of MPs **voted not to** require a report on the impact of government policy on river pollution on sentient animals
“The Animal Sentience Committee shall produce a report on the impact of government policy on river pollution on sentient animals.
(1) The annual report must include—
(a) the number of sentient animals killed or injured as a result of polluted rivers.
(b) a description of the actions of water companies to guarantee the protection of sentient animals.
(c) an assessment of the effect of government policy on (a) and (b).
(2) The first annual report on the impact of polluted rivers on sentient animals may relate to any 12 month period that includes the day on which this section comes into force.
(3) The annual report must be published and laid before Parliament within 4 months of the last day of the period to which the report relates.”—(Tim Farron.)
This new clause would require the Animal Sentience Committee to produce a report on the impact of polluted rivers on sentient animals.
Brought up.

# New clause 3 - Report on the use of sentient animals in animal experimentation in government policy
## **Votes in this debate**
*   Division number 214
A majority of MPs **voted not to** require a report, and recommendations, on the adverse effects on the welfare of animals of government policy on experimentation on animals.
‘(1) The Animal Sentience Committee shall produce a report under section 2 on the adverse effects on the welfare of animals of government policy on experimentation on animals.
(2) The report shall cover both animal experimentation where alternative (non-animal based) methods of testing exist, and where no alternative exists.
(3) The report shall cover—
(a) medical testing,
(b) cosmetics testing, and
(c) weapons testing.
(4) This report shall include recommendations for future government action under section 2 (3) and (4).’—(Deidre Brock.)

# New clause 3 - Report on the use of sentient animals in animal experimentation in government policy
## **Votes in this debate**
*   Division number 214
A majority of MPs **voted not to** require a report, and recommendations, on the adverse effects on the welfare of animals of government policy on experimentation on animals.
‘(1) The Animal Sentience Committee shall produce a report under section 2 on the adverse effects on the welfare of animals of government policy on experimentation on animals.
(2) The report shall cover both animal experimentation where alternative (non-animal based) methods of testing exist, and where no alternative exists.
(3) The report shall cover—
(a) medical testing,
(b) cosmetics testing, and
(c) weapons testing.
(4) This report shall include recommendations for future government action under section 2 (3) and (4).’—(Deidre Brock.)
Brought up.
Question put, That the clause be added to the Bill.
